title: Status webhook retry guidance and incident micro-update
summary: Micro-update for status page + follow-up customer-facing post-incident note. Includes pragmatic webhook retry guidance and a short verification checklist customers can use to validate they received all replays and notifications.
body:
Status page micro-update (post immediately):

Summary: We experienced a degraded webhook delivery path for tenant notification webhooks between 2026-09-26 22:14 UTC and 2026-09-26 22:58 UTC. Most webhook deliveries succeeded; approximately 0.4% of webhook deliveries to customer endpoints experienced transient 5xx or connection timeouts. We have completed a progressive recovery and deliveries are now normal.

What we changed (brief):
- Rolled back a routing change in the webhook dispatcher that was causing misordered backoff windows.
- Forced a resend of queued webhook notifications for affected tenants (resends were idempotent).
- Added additional health checks and telemetry to alert earlier for delivery error spikes.

Customer-facing post-incident summary (send as follow-up email / extended status page entry):

Headline: Brief outage in tenant webhook delivery — queued resends completed and verification options available

Impact: Between 22:14 and 22:58 UTC on 2026-09-26, automated outbound webhooks for tenant notifications (webhook delivery subsystem) experienced increased delivery failures to a small subset of customer endpoints. Observed symptoms included 502/504 responses and TLS handshake timeouts when Redwood attempted to post event payloads. About 0.4% of webhook attempts were not accepted by receivers and were queued for retry. No inference API requests, token usage, or embedding generation were impacted.

Root cause (tl;dr): A recent change to the webhook dispatcher routing table introduced a timing edge where some backend worker retry timers reset incorrectly, causing clustered retry attempts and occasional transient overload on the delivery mesh. This surfaced as an increase in connection/tls timeouts and 5xx responses from intermediate delivery proxies.

Timeline (UTC):
- 22:12 — Deployment of routing change to webhook dispatcher (canary starts).
- 22:14 — Telemetry alerts: webhook success rate drop and delivery error spike.
- 22:18 — On-call paged, mitigation plan started (pause deploy, roll back routing change).
- 22:26 — Rollback initiated; dispatcher rollback completed 22:30.
- 22:35 — Backlog of queued deliveries observed; automated resends began.
- 22:58 — Resends finished for queued webhook attempts. Monitoring returned to baseline.

Mitigation and verification steps taken by Redwood:
- Immediate rollback of the routing change to restore stable backoff behavior.
- Replayed queued webhook events with idempotency keys to avoid duplicate processing by customers.
- Alerted platform operators; added temporary elevated sampling of webhook failures for 48 hours.
- Instrumented dispatchers to surface per-tenant delivery latencies and per-endpoint TLS handshake errors.

Customer action checklist (recommended):
- If you run webhook endpoints, verify receipt of events between 22:12–22:58 UTC on 2026-09-26. You should have either received the original event or a queued resend (same idempotency id).
- If you have an internal audit or replay process, search by header X-Redwood-Event-Id and X-Redwood-Idempotency.
- If you use rate-limited endpoints, ensure your retry/backoff logic can accept Redwood resends (we use exponential backoff and include idempotency keys).
- If you see missing events, open a ticket with Support including one sample event id and your webhook endpoint URL.

How to verify (quick):
- Check your server logs for POST requests from Redwood's webhook IPs (see tenant ops reference).
- Example header we include: X-Redwood-Event-Id: rwd_evt_2026_09_26_0001 and X-Redwood-Idempotency: rwd_idemp_abc123
- Sample success log line to look for:
  [2026-09-26T22:36:12Z] INFO Received POST /webhook 200 X-Redwood-Event-Id=rwd_evt_2026_09_26_0001 X-Redwood-Idempotency=rwd_idemp_abc123
- Sample sign of a missing delivery (client-side): repeated connection timeouts or 5xx responses from Redwood's webhook sender during the window above.

Webhook authoring and retry guidance (for engineering contacts):
- Redwood behavior: we post with a maximum of 8 attempts per event using an exponential backoff (initial delay 2s, multiplier 2x, jitter ±20%). After final failure we persist the event and alert ops for manual re-delivery as part of this incident path.
- Recommended customer behavior: accept idempotent deliveries (use X-Redwood-Event-Id or X-Redwood-Idempotency to dedupe). Implement a tolerance to accept delayed deliveries for at least 5 minutes beyond expected time window.

Example payload (as sent in POST body):
{
  "event": "inference.completed",
  "tenant_id": "tnt_12345",
  "request_id": "req_7890",
  "timestamp": "2026-09-26T22:34:57Z",
  "result": { "tokens": 128, "cost_usd": 0.0023 }
}

Example curl for idempotent local testing (customers):
curl -X POST https://your-endpoint.example/webhook \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Event-Id: rwd_evt_2026_09_26_0001" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Idempotency: rwd_idemp_abc123" \n  -d '{"event":"inference.completed","tenant_id":"tnt_12345"}'

Suggested customer retry policy (simple):
- On 5xx or connection timeout: retry with exponential backoff, initial wait 1s, multiplier 2x, jitter ±10%, up to 6 attempts. Ensure idempotency key is used for deduping.

Server-side best practices we recommend to customers:
- Return 2xx as soon as the payload is accepted (enqueue for processing), to avoid blocking Redwood's retry budget.
- If processing fails, return a 202 and provide a retry header (preferably Link header with guidance) rather than a 500 that triggers immediate Redwood retry.
- Maintain request logs keyed by X-Redwood-Event-Id for easy reconciliation.

Internal notes to ops / follow-up items (to include in internal postmortem):
- Add a canary-level metric to detect clustered retry timers where >5 retries are scheduled within <10s window per worker.
- Fix dispatcher race condition that reset backoff timer on policy re-evaluation.
- Backfill telemetry for the 30-day window to identify tenants who saw elevated TLS handshake failures.

Q&A (for FAQ section in status page follow-up):
Q: Will I be charged twice for a replayed webhook event?
A: No. Webhook events are notifications only; they do not affect usage billing. Any backend resends are idempotent and carry the same ids.

Q: If I already processed an event, could I receive a duplicate?
A: Possibly, if your endpoint returned non-2xx for the first attempt. We provide idempotency keys to dedupe.

Q: Did this incident affect inference correctness or latency for API calls?
A: No. This was isolated to outbound webhook delivery. Inference API, embeddings, and streaming were unaffected.

Contact and escalation:
- For immediate verification requests, open a support ticket referencing INC-4321.
- For engineering verification or to request an evidence bundle, email partner-ops@redwood.ai and include sample event ids and your webhook URL.

Notes-to-self / draft markers:
- Confirm list of IP ranges we used for delivery during the window and add to this doc before final publish.
- Attach evidence bundle (delivery logs + sample payloads) to ticket response for enterprise customers who request them.
- Decide whether to include auto-retry toggles in Console (product/ux to weigh in).

Appendix — small sample of delivery log lines (internal):
[22:15:03.112] WARN dispatcher worker-7 post failed POST https://partner.example/webhook status=504 tls_handshake_timeout event=rwd_evt_2026_09_26_0041 idempotency=rwd_idemp_zz9
[22:16:07.455] INFO dispatcher worker-7 queued resend event=rwd_evt_2026_09_26_0041 attempts=1
[22:26:18.003] INFO dispatcher roll back routing-change deploy=webhook-dispatcher@v2.3.1
[22:35:44.900] INFO resend-scheduler replayed event=rwd_evt_2026_09_26_0041 attempts=3 status=accepted

End of draft.

Links to internal artifacts: INC-4321 (investigation), infra PR #987 (rollback fix branch).

-- Asha (CS on-call)
